notes: Prefer common Indonesian used in daily conversation, but keep grammar teachable.
Use colloquial forms only when they are genuinely common and context-appropriate.
Do not turn every sentence into slang.
When a target is formal/bookish, teach the natural spoken counterpart explicitly instead of pretending both registers are identical.

spoken_pairs.note: Use nggak/enggak in dialogue, tidak in neutral reading unless target register suggests otherwise.
udah is very common in dialogue.
taruh is more common in daily speech.
download is extremely common in tech contexts.
upload is extremely common in tech contexts.
enak is the normal daily word for tasty.
sambil is much more natural in ordinary conversation.
mencret is colloquial; diare suits medical/neutral contexts.
password is very common in casual tech talk.

anti_patterns: Do not put semantically unrelated target words into one sentence only to increase coverage.
Do not overuse lalu/kemudian in every sentence.
Do not use formal connectors such as dengan demikian repeatedly in casual dialogue.
Do not translate Chinese word order literally.
Do not make every dialogue line a textbook-complete sentence; short natural replies are allowed.
Do not use slang that the learner has never seen merely to sound local.
